question: Who among the following was the first Indian woman to become the President of Indian National Congress? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Nelli Sengupta
Annie Besant
Madam Bhikaji Cama
Sarojini Naidu
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sarojini Naidu

Explanation:
Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman to become the President of the Indian National Congress (INC). She was elected as the Congress President in 1925 at the Kanpur session. She was a renowned poet and freedom fighter, famously known as the 'Nightingale of India'. Later, she also became the first woman Governor of a state in India, serving as the Governor of the United Provinces (now Uttar Pradesh). Annie Besant was of British origin, not Indian. Madam Bhikaji Cama was a revolutionary, not a Congress President. Nelli Sengupta was a politician from Bengal.

☛ Which state's first woman Governor was Sarojini Naidu? → United Provinces (Uttar Pradesh)

question: The signatories of the Poona Pact were the Mahatma Gandhi Group and the _________. (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (09/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Subhas Chandra Bose Group
Jawaharlal Nehru Group
Dr. BR Ambedkar Group
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Group
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dr. BR Ambedkar Group

Explanation:
The Poona Pact was signed on 24 September 1932 between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. This agreement was reached after Gandhi's fast unto death against the Communal Award (1932). Under the pact, separate electorates for the depressed classes were replaced by reserved seats. It provided increased representation for the depressed classes in the provincial legislatures and also reserved seats in the central legislature. The Poona Pact was a significant milestone in Indian politics, bridging the differences between Gandhi and Ambedkar's approaches to the welfare of the depressed classes.

☛ Signatories of the Pact → Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
☛ Outcome of the Pact → Reserved seats for depressed classes, no separate electorates
☛ Gandhi's fast → At Yerwada Jail against the Communal Award
☛ Impact of the Pact → Increased representation for depressed classes in provincial assemblies

question: Who among the social reformers following founded the Widow Remarriage Association in 1861? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (12/12/2024) Shift 1)

Explanation:

He was a prominent social reformer and judge who worked for widow remarriage, women's education, and ending caste discrimination. Ranade was associated with the Prarthana Samaj and founded multiple organizations for social reforms. This association was established to encourage widow remarriage and their social rehabilitation. During that time, widows faced severe social hardships, and Ranade advocated for their rights. His efforts played a significant role in the social reform movement of 19th-century India.

question: In which of the following years was the All India Muslim League founded? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (12/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: 1906
1919
1905
1914
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1906

Explanation:
The All India Muslim League was founded on December 30, 1906 in Dhaka, now in Bangladesh. Its main aim was to safeguard the political rights of Indian Muslims. Key founders included Nawab Salimullah Khan, Aga Khan, Mohsin-ul-Mulk, and Waqar-ul-Mulk. The formation was largely a reaction to the partition of Bengal (1905) and the growing political consciousness among Muslims. The year 1906 also saw the rise of the Extremist faction within the Indian National Congress. The League held its first session in 1907. It played a pivotal role in the creation of Pakistan, especially after the Lahore Resolution of 1940. Thus, the correct year is 1906.

☛ Who was the Viceroy of India in 1906? → Lord Minto

question: Who among the following established the Atmiya Sabha in 1815? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (12/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Raja Rammohan Roy

Keshub Chandra Sen

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Raja Rammohan Roy

Explanation:
Raja Rammohan Roy established the Atmiya Sabha in 1815 in Kolkata. It marked the beginning of the socio-religious reform movement in India. The Sabha aimed to promote monotheism (belief in one God) and raise voice against social evils like Sati, child marriage, and caste discrimination. Discussions on Vedic scriptures and rational debates were held in the Sabha. Later, in 1828, Raja Rammohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj, which was an extension of the Atmiya Sabha.

question: Who is most commonly associated with the 'safety valve' theory regarding the formation of the Indian National Congress? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (09/06/2025) Shift 3)

Explanation:
The 'safety valve' theory regarding the formation of the Indian National Congress is most commonly associated with AO Hume. This theory suggests that the British government, through Hume, created the Congress as a platform to channel the growing discontent among Indians in a controlled manner, thus acting as a safety valve to prevent any large-scale uprising. However, many historians reject this theory, arguing that it undermines the genuine nationalist sentiment and the efforts of Indian leaders who sought a political platform for their demands.

कोया विद्रोह (1840-1845) आंध्र प्रदेश के गोदावरी और विशाखापत्तनम जिलों में हुआ था। इसका मुख्य कारण अंग्रेजों द्वारा आदिवासियों को ताड़ी के पेड़ों पर उनके पारंपरिक अधिकारों से वंचित करना था। अंग्रेजों ने ताड़ी के पेड़ों पर अपना नियंत्रण स्थापित कर लिया था, जिससे आदिवासियों की आजीविका प्रभावित हुई। कोया जनजाति ने इस शोषण के खिलाफ विद्रोह किया। अन्य विकल्प: खासी विद्रोह (1833) मेघालय में हुआ था और इसका कारण अंग्रेजों की विस्तारवादी नीति थी। तेलांगा खारिया विद्रोह झारखंड में हुआ था और इसका कारण जंगल कानून थे। मांझी विद्रोह का ताड़ी के पेड़ों से कोई संबंध नहीं था।
